title: I Owe Tomorrow to Someone I Haven't Met
subtitle: Aspect · Character trouble · two-edged authoring example

fields.label: Meaning
fields.value: A binding promise saved you once. Its unknown holder can someday demand repayment, but that promise also marks you as someone trusted by an unusual future ally.

fields.label: Useful applications
fields.value: Invoke when that obligation gives you credibility with time-brokers, or when you draw on preparations made to honor the promise. Explain relevance and pay or use a valid free invoke normally.

fields.label: Complication applications
fields.value: A compel could bring a repayment demand during a rescue, or reveal that a useful official is the debt holder whose interests oppose yours. Negotiate the complication; it does not force a player action or mean a roll must fail.

fields.label: Not a power
fields.value: The aspect alone does not grant prophecy, time travel or a standing +2. Establish supernatural permissions separately.

fields.label: Connected use
fields.value: This is Ira Venn's trouble. Decide who holds the debt through play or with the player, not by secretly rewriting established history.
